exercise.name: Resistance Band Standing External Rotation
aliases: Standing band external rotation, elbow at the side

reference.title: Resistance Band Standing External Rotation
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (the proxy refused gymvisual.com), so the movement follows the name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you rotate up, breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s up, short pause, about 2 s down

prescription.progression: Add reps, then 0.5-1 kg; longer pause at the top

cues.text: Stand side-on to the anchor, band at elbow height on the side away from the working arm. Elbow bent 90 degrees and tucked by the side (a rolled towel helps), thumb up, hand in front of the belly.
Breathe out and turn the forearm out like a gate, keeping the elbow against the side.
Stop when the forearm points about 45-60 degrees out, before the elbow leaves the side; shoulder blade back and down.
Breathe in and let the hand come back across the belly slowly against the band.
Brief pause, then repeat. Turn around to train the other arm.

mistakes.mistake: Elbow drifting away from the side
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbow tucked (squeeze a towel roll); stop the turn earlier.

mistakes.mistake: Turning the trunk instead of the arm
mistakes.fix: Keep the hips and shoulders square; only the forearm moves.

mistakes.mistake: Bending the wrist back to finish the range
mistakes.fix: Keep the wrist straight; the turn comes from the shoulder.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the band snap the hand back

kinematics.norm: By the side (0-20 degrees of abduction; a towel roll under the arm is common), still through the rep (clinical opinion); Sung 2023 tested external rotation at 45 and 90 degrees of abduction
From the forearm across the belly to about 45-60 degrees out, as far as the elbow stays put (clinical opinion)

Elastic tension rises as the band stretches, so the load is highest where the band is longest; at matched effort, elastic tubing and dumbbells gave similar muscle activity in upper-body exercises (Andersen 2010); anchored to the opposite side at elbow height, the band pulls the hand back across the body, so it resists the whole turn out
Slow, about 2 s each way (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #18909, Resistance Band Standing External Rotation, video (movement reference)
Sung, Jung, Wang and Kim 2023, the effects of body positions and abduction angles on shoulder muscle activity patterns during external rotation exercises (Healthcare 11(14):1977)

Andersen, Andersen, Mortensen, Poulsen, Bjornlund and Zebis 2010, muscle activation and perceived loading during rehabilitation exercises: comparison of dumbbells and elastic resistance (Phys Ther 90(4):538-549)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a catching feeling, numbness or tingling occurs.
Check the band for nicks or tears before each set and make sure it cannot slip off its anchor (under the feet, round the upright).
Use a light band: the rotator cuff is small and this is a control exercise, not a strength test.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Pain at the end of the turn: shorten the range.
Hard to keep the elbow still: put a rolled towel between the elbow and the ribs.
regressions: Lighter band, or step closer to the anchor.
Side-lying external rotation with no load.
progressions: External rotation at 90 degrees of abduction (as in the dumbbell standing external rotation).

muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Prime mover (with teres minor): turns the upper arm out. External rotation exercises target it; Sung 2023 found body position and abduction angle change how much it works (tested at 45 and 90 degrees).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Helps turn the arm out (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Hold the shoulder blade back as the arm turns out (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Holds the small gap between the elbow and the ribs.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Keeps the shoulder blade on the ribs.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk square so it does not turn with the arm.
muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_r: Hold the wrist straight against the band.
